Running club note, Sunday
Darshan has become one of my steadiest runners this year, and I think I know why. After our long run he always stays for the full breakfast at the tea stall, sits for an hour, eats slowly and talks to everyone. He clearly enjoys it; he says it's the best part of his week. Last night the younger runners planned a midnight bike ride to the hills and a second breakfast after. He laughed, said it sounded brilliant, and said no; he had an early shift and wanted to be rested. He came to the run this morning fresh and ran his best time. I've asked him to lead the Sunday breakfast talk next month.
– Madhav, coach

qa.a: He said no because of his early shift and wanting rest, and he came fresh to the run and ran his best time.

qa.a: They may be a bit disappointed, but seeing him laugh and still enjoy breakfast shows them fun and rest can go together.

Saturday night
Today was good in a slow way. I'm Nilesh, and I'm writing it down so I remember. I cooked rajma from scratch, no hurry, and Tarun came over to eat. We played carrom for two hours and I lost every game. Then we walked to the lake and just sat. Around eight, Tarun got a call about a party across town, the third one this week. Part of me wanted to go; parties are fun. But I've got my cousin's wedding prep tomorrow and I've been tired all week. I said no, and Tarun went. I'm on my balcony now with a cup of tea, full and happy. I don't need more tonight. This was enough.

qa.q: How long did Nilesh and Tarun play carrom?
qa.a: For two hours.

qa.q: How does Nilesh feel at the end of the day on the balcony?
qa.a: Nilesh feels full, calm and happy, content with a slow day without needing more excitement.

qa.q: Which choice kept Nilesh's day in balance?
qa.a: Nilesh said no to the third party of the week because of tiredness and wedding prep, keeping joy without letting pleasure take over.

qa.q: What would change if Nilesh had gone to the party too?
qa.a: Nilesh might have enjoyed it, but would probably be worn out for the wedding prep and lose the calm, content feeling of the day.

grounding: A diary entry shows an adult savouring a slow day of cooking, games and friends, and turning down more partying to stay rested.

On Sundays in Nabha, Simran, twenty-five, a schoolteacher, took joy seriously. She and her friend Rekha rode to the dhaba on the highway and ate slowly: makki roti, saag, a glass of lassi each, and an hour of talking about nothing.
Then Simran napped under the fan with the window open. In the evening she flew kites on the roof with her nephews, shrieking when the string cut.
At eight Rekha called. "The mela is still on! Last night, come, we'll stay till midnight."
Simran laughed. "I've had the best day. And I'm on exam duty at seven tomorrow."
"You're so boring."
"I'm so happy," Simran said, and meant it. "Go. Bring me back jalebis."
She ironed her sari for the morning, listening to the mela music float over the rooftops, and didn't feel she had missed anything.

qa.q: What did Simran and Rekha eat at the dhaba?
qa.a: Makki roti, saag and a glass of lassi each.

qa.q: How did Simran feel as she listened to the mela music while ironing?
qa.a: She felt happy and content, not left out, because she had already enjoyed her day fully.

qa.q: Which choice showed Simran balancing joy with her commitments?
qa.a: Turning down the late mela because of exam duty at seven, after a day of food, rest and play, showed she values pleasure without letting it override her work.

qa.q: How does Rekha see Simran's choice?
qa.a: Rekha teases her as boring, seeing only the missed fun, not how full Simran's day already was.

grounding: It shows an adult who takes real time for meals, rest and play and keeps pleasure in balance with her commitments instead of chasing more.

Saturday in Nairobi was Wanjiru's slow day, and she guarded it. She walked to the market without her phone, bought mangoes and sukuma wiki, and stopped to watch a man play guitar outside the bakery. At home she cooked for two hours, music loud, and ate on the balcony with her neighbour Vera.
In the evening they went to a friend's birthday. Wanjiru danced until her feet hurt, laughing at her own terrible moves.
At eleven Vera grabbed her arm. "After-party in Westlands! Everyone's going."
Wanjiru hesitated. It sounded fun. But she was helping at her aunt's shop at eight, and she had promised to walk her cousin through a job form after.
"Not tonight," she said. "Tonight was perfect already."
She took a matatu home, humming, and fell asleep with the taste of mango still in her mouth.

qa.q: What did Wanjiru buy at the market?
qa.a: Mangoes and sukuma wiki.

qa.q: What was Wanjiru feeling when she hesitated about the after-party?
qa.a: She was tempted because it sounded fun, but she also felt satisfied and mindful of her promises for the next morning.

qa.q: What choice did Wanjiru make, and why was it a wise balance?
qa.a: She skipped the after-party after enjoying the whole day, keeping her commitments to her aunt and cousin without giving up joy.

qa.q: How might Vera see Wanjiru leaving early?
qa.a: Vera might be a little disappointed to lose her friend's company, but she has shared much of Wanjiru's good day and may respect her choice.

grounding: It shows an adult who takes real time for meals, music and dancing but keeps pleasure in balance with her commitments instead of chasing the next thrill.
